preferred_candidate_source_family.name: PyThaiNLP Thai word-list/newmm source family with clean-room TCC or TCC+ boundary rules
reasoning: PyThaiNLP is a maintained Thai NLP project with public repository history, public documentation, and documented dictionary-based newmm tokenization behavior.
PyThaiNLP documentation identifies thai_words() as the base word set used by newmm revision utilities and links the word-list identity to words_th.txt.

PyThaiNLP documentation exposes TCC, TCC+ and ETCC behavior as subword tokenization choices, giving reviewable behavior references while still requiring a clean-room project-owned rule implementation.

The source family is suitable for a first candidate lock because it can be evaluated as dictionary-based Thai segmentation constrained by explicit subword boundaries without committing data or adapter code in this task.
not_selected_alternatives: ICU dictionary data is not selected because this task needs an exact redistributable source chain before any dictionary data or tokenizer adapter is introduced.
Volubilis-derived word lists are not selected for the first candidate because the observed corpus-license chain includes CC-BY-SA language that needs a separate redistribution decision.
JTCC grammar or PyThaiNLP regex/rule code is not selected as implementation material because this task requires clean-room TCC/TCC+ work before adapter coding.

remaining_no_go_conditions_before_adapte: Do not download, vendor, commit, or transform words_th.txt or any other Thai dictionary rows until the exact artifact identity and license chain are approved.
Do not copy PyThaiNLP, JTCC, tccseg, ICU, or other third-party tokenizer implementation code, regexes, grammars, generated tables, or rule data without a separate approval.
Do not bundle CC-BY-SA or other reciprocal dictionary data without explicit compatibility, attribution, notice, and redistribution approval.
Do not register thai_dictionary_tcc_v1 or claim real Thai segmentation until deterministic token stream fixtures and search regressions pass.
Do not allow runtime network fetches for dictionary, TCC/TCC+, license, or model resources.
Do not use unpinned branches, mutable URLs, or undocumented generated artifacts as tokenizer sources.
Do not describe fallback CJK bigrams or synthetic non-space readiness fixtures as Thai word segmentation.
Do not proceed without maintainer/legal signoff for GPL-2.0-or-later compatibility and WordPress.org package redistribution.

future_verification_plan.tokenizer_fixture_requirement: Add deterministic Thai token stream fixtures covering offsets, positions, TCC/TCC+ boundary constraints, longest-match dictionary tie breaks, unknown Thai runs, mixed scripts, and malformed UTF-8 rejection.
future_verification_plan.search_regression_requirement: Add Thai search fixtures for phrase matching, highlighting, AND/OR behavior, unknown terms, ranking, and explicit no-fuzzy behavior if the tokenizer disables fuzzy expansion.
future_verification_plan.performance_requirement: Gate dictionary load memory, trie build time, maximum Thai run bytes, maximum generated rows, and index/search time on representative Thai documents before enabling the adapter.
